equity_bridge.item: Equity-method investments (pipeline JVs) at ~10x FY2025 distributions of $397m; book $3,139m at 2026-06-30
equity_bridge.note: Equity earnings are excluded from CSV EBITDA (operating income + D&A), so the asset is added here per the matching-asset rule. Q2 2026 10-Q, FY2025 10-K cash flow statement.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: post-integration organic EBITDA growth (management: mid-to-high single digit for 5-7 years, haircut) decelerating to 2.5% terminal; historical CAGRs are M&A-driven
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR 51.5% vs revenue 14.5% / EPS 12.2%: equity nearly tripled because Magellan (Sep-2023), Medallion (Oct-2024) and EnLink (Oct-2024/Jan-2025) were part-paid in stock (shares 448m -> 632m). Revenue 5yr CAGR of 31.5% is the same acquisitions plus commodity pass-through. None of the historical CAGRs describe the organic run-rate; the forward path is anchored to guidance instead.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF less SBC): FY2022 $1,651m -> FY2025 $2,355m = 12.6% vs reported 12.8%; 5yr undefined because FY2020 owner FCF was negative (-$325m, Elk Creek/Arbuckle II build). SBC is ~0.3% of revenue so owner and reported series are nearly identical. Base years: FY2020 revenue $8,542m, FY2022 $22,387m, FY2025 $33,629m; EPS 1.42 / 3.85 / 5.43; equity $6,043m / $6,494m / $22,569m.

scenario_narratives.base: ONEOK as a ~90% fee-based, integrated NGL/refined-products/gas platform post Magellan-Medallion-EnLink. FY2026 tracks the twice-raised guidance ($8.35bn adj. EBITDA). Growth decelerates from ~6% to ~3% as the 2024-27 project wave (Elk Creek expansion, West Texas NGL, Medford/Denver fractionation, Permian gas pipelines, Texas City LPG export) is absorbed, then 2.5% nominal from tariff escalators. Capex falls from ~$3bn to the guided $2.0-2.5bn run-rate; the resulting FCF deleverages toward 3.5x. Cash taxes rise from ~2% to 24% as bonus depreciation on a shrinking capex base runs down. Terminal value capped at 15x owner FCF.
scenario_narratives.bull: Operating momentum (record Permian and NGL throughput, second 2026 guidance raise) persists: EBITDA compounds at the management-guided mid-to-high single digits for five years, cost and commercial synergies exceed $450m, and gas-for-power/AI data-centre supply agreements add a new contracted vertical. Lower capex intensity and a longer tax shelter lift owner-FCF margins toward 12%; exit at 16x owner FCF (~9x EBITDA), still inside the midstream peer range.
scenario_narratives.bear: Scale does not insulate from recontracting: Bakken NGL volumes migrate to Kinder Morgan, Mid-Con G&P volumes erode, and a soft NGL/gas tape compresses the residual commodity-exposed margins and slows producer activity feeding the gathering systems. Integration of three overlapping deals obscures organic performance; synergies arrive late. EBITDA grows ~1.5%/yr, capex stays elevated, leverage lingers above 4x and the exit multiple de-rates to 12x owner FCF.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Unlevered owner-FCF DCF on consolidated EBITDA excluding equity-method earnings, with the JV stakes added back in the bridge at ~10x distributions and all interest-bearing debt (including commercial paper) deducted. SBC is expensed and the count held flat. The cash-tax shelter from bonus depreciation is explicitly run off to a 24% rate by year 10 rather than perpetuated. Risk is carried in the scenario flows and the 25/50/25 weights, not in a scenario-specific WACC. Terminal value is capped at 12-16x owner FCF (roughly 7-9x EBITDA), below the current midstream trading range, so the valuation does not depend on multiple expansion.
key_risks_to_valuation: Leverage: ~$33bn of debt at ~4.2x EBITDA; a 100bp rise in refinancing cost is ~$330m/yr of equity cash flow and would pressure the BBB rating
Recontracting/competitive bypass (Bakken NGL volumes to Kinder Morgan) in basins where ONEOK has historically held dominant share
Residual commodity exposure through percent-of-proceeds, keep-whole and marketing/optimisation margins; a sustained low NGL/gas tape also slows producer volumes
Integration execution across Magellan, Medallion and EnLink; synergy capture below the $450m+ run-rate
Cash-tax normalisation arriving sooner than modelled if capex falls faster than bonus depreciation can shelter
Revenue is commodity pass-through, so the revenue growth path is a weak anchor; the valuation rests on the EBITDA and capex paths
Equity-method stakes valued at ~10x distributions ($3.97bn) in the bridge; at book ($3.14bn) the weighted value is ~$1.3/share lower

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API regular close at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 64.02-99.85
data_sources.financials: OKE_Metrics.csv (SEC XBRL, FY2007-Q2 2026) for revenue, operating income, EBITDA, OCF, capex, SBC, equity, shares; SEC companyfacts XBRL (CIK 1039684) read directly for the FY2025 10-K and Q2 2026 10-Q component lines: debt tranches, cash, NCI, equity-method investments and distributions, D&A, interest paid ($1,732m), income taxes paid ($74m), dividends ($2,583m), repurchases ($75m), diluted shares
data_sources.qualitative: OKE_Analysis.json (2026-10-02): Q2 2026 guidance (adj. EBITDA $8.35bn midpoint, capex $2.7-3.2bn, $2.0-2.5bn run-rate from 2027, mid-to-high-single-digit EBITDA growth 5-7 years), bull/bear axes

inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2025 (Dec year-end) consolidated revenue, $m. Revenue is largely commodity pass-through (NGL/crude/refined-products marketing), so the year-1 growth of ~24% is the H1-2026 run-rate (H1-26 $21,667m vs H1-25 $15,930m) annualising to ~$41.7bn, not volume growth; EBITDA margin is set per year to deliver the EBITDA path, which is the line that matters.
inputs.debt_note: 2026-06-30 10-Q: long-term debt non-current $30,773m + current maturities $750m + commercial paper/short-term borrowings $1,499m = $33,022m; cash $161m. The Metrics.csv total_debt of $32,250m omits the current maturities. Operating lease liabilities ($237m at 2025-12-31) excluded: US GAAP operating lease cost is already inside EBITDA (treatment B).
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash flow statement share-based compensation add-back ($92m; FY2024 $102m). No separate equity-award tax withholding line disclosed; SBC is 0.27% of revenue so the omission is immaterial.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 repurchases $75m (FY2024 $159m) against $2.6bn of dividends; the flat count is a modelling convention, funded only partly by buybacks. SBC is expensed in the flows so the count is held flat (charge once).
inputs.share_count_basis: Weighted-average diluted shares, Q2 2026 10-Q (632.0m); cover-page basic count 630.4m at 2026-07-27. Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Rf 4.2% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, beta ~1.0 -> cost of equity 9.2%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~5.6% (BBB/Baa2 recent issuance), after-tax ~4.3%. Debt ~37% of EV ($33.0bn debt vs ~$55bn market cap) -> WACC 7.4%, used as 7.5%. Same WACC in all three scenarios: leverage, commodity and recontracting risk are priced in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked into the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B): operating lease cost is an operating expense inside EBITDA under US GAAP; lease liabilities ($237m) excluded from net debt. Finance leases immaterial.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interests $100m at 2026-06-30 (post EnLink buy-in Jan-2025; was $5.1bn at 2024-12-31) deducted in the equity bridge; flows modelled at 100% consolidated. NCI share of FY2025 net income was $69m, trending to ~$3m/half in 2026.
inputs.equity_method_note: CSV EBITDA = operating income + D&A ($5,741m + $1,514m = $7,255m FY2025) and EXCLUDES equity-method earnings ($386m FY2025; distributions $397m). Matching-asset rule: the investments (Northern Border, Overland Pass, Roadrunner, BridgeTex, Saddlehorn etc.; book $3,139m at 2026-06-30) are added in the equity bridge at ~10x trailing distributions = $3,970m instead.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (unlevered), routed per dcf-methods SKILL.md as an operating company, cyclical/capex-heavy row (owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md: leases, NCI, matching-asset rule, charge-risk-once). ONEOK is a C-corp, ~90% fee-based midstream; cash flows are a stream of owner FCF so the standard engine applies. Not an MLP/AFFO case. FY0 = FY2025 actuals; year 1 = FY2026 (guidance year: adj. EBITDA $8.35bn midpoint, raised twice; on the CSV basis ex equity earnings and SBC that is ~$7.88bn, consistent with H1-26 $3,786m). Cash taxes: $74m paid in FY2025 vs $1,028m provision (bonus depreciation, now permanent under OBBBA); the shelter is NOT perpetuated -- the cash rate ramps to 24% (federal 21% + state) by year 10. Capex per management: $2.7-3.2bn 2026, $2.0-2.5bn run-rate from 2027 as Elk Creek/West Texas NGL/Permian gas and LPG export projects complete. Net debt is the 2026-06-30 balance (net debt rose ~$120m from 2025-12-31 despite H1 FCF, as dividends absorbed it), so using FY2026 as year 1 does not materially double-count H1 flows.

bear.narrative: FY2026 lands at the low end ($7.63bn CSV basis) and EBITDA then grows ~1.5%/yr: Bakken NGL volumes lost to Kinder Morgan on contract roll-off, Mid-Con/Rockies G&P volumes flat-to-down, POP/keep-whole and marketing margins compress in a low NGL-price tape, synergies partly offset by integration costs. Capex stays near $2.5bn as maintenance and recontracting-defence spend rises; cash taxes normalise faster; leverage stays above 4x so the market pays 12x owner FCF (~7x EBITDA) at exit.

base.narrative: EBITDA (CSV basis) $7.88bn FY2026 (guidance) -> $8.35bn -> $8.77bn -> $9.1bn -> $9.4bn by FY2030, i.e. ~6%/5%/4%/3.5%/3% then 2.5-3% nominal (tariff escalators). Capex $2.95bn -> $2.5bn -> $2.3bn -> ~4.5% of revenue (~$2.1-2.4bn) long run, above D&A at 3.5%. Cash tax ramps 3% -> 24%. Terminal cap 15x owner FCF ~ 8.6x terminal EBITDA, below where midstream trades (9-11x).

bull.narrative: Management's mid-to-high-single-digit EBITDA growth delivered: FY2026 $8.0bn then +8.6%/+7.6%/+6%/+5%, synergies above the $450m run-rate, Permian gas takeaway and LPG export projects on time, data-centre gas supply becomes a repeatable vertical. Bonus depreciation keeps the cash tax rate low for longer; capex steps down to the bottom of the $2.0-2.5bn range.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: net debt/EBITDA is ~4.2x against a 3.5x target, the recontracting loss in the Bakken is already visible, and three large integrations are still being absorbed. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs several independent things to go right at once (synergy over-delivery, on-time Permian/LPG projects, the data-centre gas vertical scaling, and a prolonged tax shelter). Base 50%.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
